takeaway: Pain on passive stretch: anterior - plantarflex; lateral - invert; superficial posterior - dorsiflex; deep posterior - extend the great toe.

question.text: If concerned about compartment syndrome following reperfusion of the lower leg, what action would you perform in order to test the deep part of the posterior compartment of the lower leg?

lines.text: Pain on a passive stretch of a muscle is the key sign of compartment syndrome.
lines.say: (clears throat) Pain on a passive stretch of a muscle is the key sign of compartment syndrome.

lines.text: The lower leg has four compartments, and each can be tested on its own.
Anterior: plantarflex the foot. Lateral: invert it.
Deep posterior: extend the great toe.
That stretches flexor hallucis longus, in the deep posterior compartment.
Oedema blocks the veins, and pressure builds until the arterial supply fails.
So, to test the deep posterior compartment, extend the great toe.
